text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.9% today as oil prices retreated from their recent spike. Brent crude topped out above $111 yesterday on Middle East tensions (U.S. threats toward Iran, staff pullout from Saudi Arabia), but that geopolitical premium appears to have peaked—the market is now pricing in lower odds of an actual escalation. With the broader energy trade losing momentum, refinery stocks like MPC, which benefit from higher crude costs, gave back gains from the recent rally.

The stock is also caught in a longer trend: U.S. refinery utilization is running at 93.4%, near capacity, which limits how much MPC can boost profits if crude stays elevated. Separately, news about India's Reliance expanding refining capacity and potentially importing Venezuelan crude adds longer-term competitive pressure on U.S. refiners, though that's a slower-moving backdrop than today's oil price swing.
